message.content:
This is a rigid molded plastic case resembling a briefcase or attaché case, with a foam insert that is not specially shaped for any item. That points to heading 4202, which covers trunks, suitcases, vanity cases, attaché cases, briefcases, and similar containers.

Because the foam is not shaped or fitted for particular articles, the case is not a specially shaped or fitted case. This rules out the 4202.92 and similar-type classifications for fitted cases, and it also rules out heading 4202.11 and 4202.12 type cases.

The relevant subheading is 4202.92, for containers with an outer surface of plastic sheeting or textile materials. Within it, the question is whether a molded plastic case counts as "outer surface of plastic." CBP rulings on similar molded plastic tool cases have classified them under 4202.92.9026 ("Other: Other: Other").

The 4202.12 subheading covers trunks, suitcases, vanity cases, attaché cases, briefcases, school satchels and similar containers with an outer surface of plastics or textile materials. Its 4202.12.81 and 4202.12.89 numbers cover items with an outer surface of plastics. The item here is described as an attaché or briefcase type, so 4202.12 fits, with the molded-plastic-exterior line being 4202.12.8130 or a similar number.

My best classification is 4202.12.8130, the line for "Other" containers of this type with an outer surface of molded plastics. This is from memory and I have not confirmed the statistical suffix against the current schedule.
